publicLaunchBlockers.title: Production has no steady-state switch for real payments: every production preference needs the 'smoke' secret that runbooks and tooling require to be absent, and the failure happens after stock is reserved
publicLaunchBlockers.notes: SOFTWARE HALF FIXED (4b3f40f): with the production gate closed the checkout session answers 409 PAYMENTS_NOT_ENABLED and reserves nothing. WAITING ON THE OWNER: which switch enables real payments in steady state. Today production only issues a preference while the secret named 'smoke' is present, and the runbooks and tools require it to be absent. Options in the decision memo (evidence, payments.md): A, an explicit permanent project-level switch (recommended); B, rely on the project review status plus the per-business switch. Until it is decided production stays closed and fails closed. Not changed in this branch: it is the switch for real money.

entries.limits: Covers one cash delivery order end to end on staging (customer, business panel contract, rider, tracking, delivery code, idempotency, lost response, RLS, stock) at main 1358188 plus fix 62f8566, with a 158-migration ledger. It does not cover: Mercado Pago, the catalog import and publication pipeline, controlled production, or migration 20261001180000 (order intake guard), which was written after the run, so the guard is not covered by this evidence.

Not certified in any environment. The sandbox approval is blocked at the provider (WCS-51579) and needs human test accounts, and the staging certification report of 2026-10-01 records that the seller of the real store is not connected. Certifying it takes an approved sandbox payment and then the controlled real payment of docs/REAL-PAYMENT-CANARY-RUNBOOK.md.

findings.title: Panel stock edit overwrites products.stock with the counted number: reserved units ignored, no concurrency check, no ledger row; this oversells
findings.notes: The count sent by the sheet, the plan and the product form is translated like the Caja Clara count (available = max(count - reserved, 0), ledger row, stock conflict when the count does not cover the reserved units), with an optional expected_stock guard (PT409). The Panel scanner count sends only a difference against the available figure and cannot be translated: while the product has reserved units it is refused (22023, STOCK_COUNT_HAS_RESERVED) and points to the catalog count. Client follow-ups, not blocking: the Panel still prefills the count field with the available figure (errs on the safe side) and does not send expected_stock; stage_catalog_products (import_catalog_batch) still writes an absolute stock.

findings.title: No order trace contract: diagnosing one order needs service_role SQL across ~15 tables with PII
findings.notes: get_order_trace (owner/admin/staff of the business) and get_order_trace_service (service_role): identifiers, state, ordered timeline and gaps, with no PII by construction.

findings.title: A non-2xx on the merchant-order lookup turns a legitimate approved payment into a permanent security review with no recovery or refund path
findings.fixed_by: 5d0c366 (the failed read no longer records an empty preference) · 12f79b8 · 18dcb08 (a charge in review can be recovered into an order or refunded)
findings.notes: Closed in two halves. Database (18dcb08): an approved payment parked in security review without an order can be recovered into an order or refunded. Edge (5d0c366): a failed merchant-order read raises instead of recording an empty preference, so the false preference_mismatch is no longer produced. Residuals, by decision: a payment that has neither an order id nor a preference id is still recorded with an empty preference and goes to manual review (now with a recovery and a refund path); a permanent merchant-order failure (404) retries to dead_letter, which raises the CRITICAL queue alert, instead of going to manual review. Provider simulated: not exercised against real Mercado Pago.

findings.title: recover_paid_checkout_order can build an order on a payment that was already refunded, or has a refund in flight
A rejected first card attempt releases the stock, so the buyer's approved retry in the same Checkout Pro preference becomes a manual review instead of an order
findings.fixed_by: a2f6960 (a provider rejection keeps the reservation and the session) · 4d18709 (the worker finds the approved payment by the checkout reference when the pinned one is rejected)
findings.notes: Closed in two halves. Database (a2f6960): a provider rejection no longer releases the reservation nor cancels the session, and the first approved payment takes the identity. Edge (4d18709): when the pinned payment is rejected the worker looks the payment up by the checkout reference and finds the approved retry. Cost of the fix: the reservation of a rejected payment is held until the session expires. Provider simulated: the retry inside one Checkout Pro preference was not exercised against real Mercado Pago (external gate).

findings.title: Sessions parked in manual_review_required keep their 'active' reservations forever, and recover_paid_checkout_order then decrements the stock a second time

findings.title: Unpaid checkout sessions can reserve the whole catalog: no cap on concurrent open sessions, 1000 units per line, DB rate limit off by default, anonymous customers
findings.notes: Bounded by the same guard on create_checkout_session: sessions count against the customer pending cap and window shared with cash orders, a unit cap applies to any unpaid commitment, and a business ceiling applies. A reservation still holds stock until its TTL by design.

findings.title: The manual (cash/coordinate) order path enforces no rate limit, pending cap, IP check or abuse logging; max_pending_orders_per_customer is enforced by nothing on either path
findings.notes: Scope of this entry: the missing intake limits only. The aliases STK-01, PRICE-01, AUTHZ-01 and OSM-01 are carried here for that half; their other half (an unpaid order holds stock with no expiry and no automatic release) is tracked by F2. Marking F1 fixed by the order intake guard does not close F2. Closed in the branch by the central intake guard (per-customer, per-origin and per-business limits, pending caps, cooldown, defaults instead of NULL=unlimited); pgTAP order_intake_guard_test.sql and the concurrency harness scripts/order-intake/intake-race.mjs run in the CI database gate.

findings.title: A single unpaid order can take the entire public stock, holds it with no expiry, and cancellation does not republish the products
findings.fixed_by: 7bdf9d4 (unit cap and pending caps) · af0451d (cancel republishes) · 6634022 (unattended orders expire)
findings.notes: Closed in the branch. The expiry only acts when the owner sets businesses.abandoned_order_minutes; while it is NULL an unattended order still holds stock until staff cancel it, bounded by the guard caps.

findings.title: Platform verification passes without service hours or delivery zones, and both enforcement flags can be switched off after verification
findings.notes: Verification refuses without an active owner, enforced hours with a window per enabled channel and, with delivery, enforced coverage with an active zone (8ec5de2). A verified business cannot switch either enforcement off (7030f69) nor switch delivery on without coverage (0977a75, the residual door the adversarial review found). Already verified businesses are not revoked by any migration: the read-only pre-flight query for them is in the migration matrix.

findings.title: No single PRODUCTION_READY gate; opening:check reports TECHNICAL_READY without checking migration parity, Edge Function deployment, the served commit, payment certification or open P0/P1
findings.notes: One gate now evaluates catalog approval, prices, hours, zones, team, seller, payment certification, migration parity, Edge Functions, abuse protection and this register; anything unknown fails closed.

findings.title: The canonical DB gate (936 pgTAP, non-superuser migration apply, rollback drills, restore) cannot run on this notebook, and CI does not trigger for the hardening branch

findings.title: apply_inventory_movement never maintains available: taking a published product to 0 fails with a raw 23514
Cancelling or rejecting an order returns stock but never republishes, while checkout expiry and POS do; products silently stay off the storefront
inventory_movements is not a complete stock ledger: most stock changes write no movement
findings.notes: NOT CHANGED, by decision. Mitigated on this branch: catalog paths now write the catalog change trail and, when they carry a count, an inventory_movements row (142451e); the stock effects of an online order are reconstructed by get_order_trace from its lines and reservations (a39db9a); the race harness asserts conservation of units on every door (c6dac99). A single ledger row for every stock change needs the point-of-sale writers too (pos_apply_stock_movements, pos_apply_stock_count), which the Caja Clara sales-ledger line is redefining in a parallel branch: it has to be designed together with that ledger, not on top of it.

findings.title: order_items does not freeze SKU, barcode, category, alcohol flag or tax; SKU is dropped at finalization and pos_list_orders joins it live
findings.notes: PARTIAL (8e7dd77, migration 20261001225000): the SKU is frozen in the order line at insert, backfilled for existing lines and immutable afterwards. With it the order keeps every commercial field the mission lists (name, SKU, quantity, unit price, subtotal, discounts, delivery fee, total, currency). Still read live from the product: barcode, category, the alcohol flag and tax attributes, and the point-of-sale order listing joins the product. The age check of an order does not depend on it (the confirmation is frozen in the order), and the fiscal document is computed by the fiscal core. The point-of-sale listing belongs to the Caja Clara work line and was not touched here. Lead assessment of what remains: P3.

findings.title: With zone enforcement on, the delivery fee and minimum are selected by a neighbourhood string the client declares, with no check against the confirmed pin

Column-level UPDATE grants on products and businesses bypass RPC authority, validation, inventory ledger and audit
findings.notes: PARTIAL. Products half CLOSED (142451e): UPDATE on stock, available and is_active is revoked from authenticated; stock moves through the RPCs with a ledger row and publication through the RPCs with gates. Businesses half MITIGATED, not closed (91840b3, 0977a75): the column grant stays because the Panel writes some of those columns directly; every such write is now audited with before, after and actor, the currency of a verified business is locked and delivery cannot be switched on without coverage. Still true: an owner or admin can change status, fulfilment switches and contact data with a direct PATCH instead of the RPC. Closing it means moving the Panel to the RPCs and revoking the grant.

findings.title: identity_close_own_session lets any authenticated user (including an anonymous customer) append unlimited audit events to any business
Permission catalog is not the enforced contract: admin can authorize ARCA homologation, staff can cancel orders
Rate-limit key combines IP and user and takes the first x-forwarded-for hop; the unauthenticated webhook writes a row per rejected request; nothing purges the tables
findings.notes: Client address from cf-connecting-ip, separate user and address buckets, signature decided before any write, rejected receipts capped per address and overall, daily purge. Not addressed: the fixed-window double burst across a window boundary.

findings.title: Preference creation has dead ends: any provider 4xx (including 408/409/429) marks the attempt failed with no way to open a new one; local errors are recorded as provider timeouts; ambiguous attempts are never resolved
findings.notes: PARTIAL (5b247f7): a provider 408/409/425/429 leaves the attempt uncertain instead of failed, and local errors send nothing and record nothing. Still open, needs a decision: an uncertain attempt answers 202 until the session expires and is never re-sent; a final 4xx leaves the intent in preference_creating with no way to open a new attempt. Options: re-POST with the same idempotency key after a provably empty search, and/or a database exit.

findings.title: The seller credential is destroyed on non-authoritative provider signals: any HTTP 401 on any resource, and any ambiguous refresh outcome
findings.notes: A resource 401 is confirmed against /users/me before the credential is invalidated; an ambiguous refresh keeps the credential and is marked for attention. Residual: a connection can stay 'connected' with an expired token if the refresh keeps failing through the token's last day, and availability does not look at the expiry (database change, not done); no alert reads the pending-refresh marker.

Business refusals raised with SQLSTATE 55000 are answered as HTTP 500 by the API, and the Panel outbox treats every status >= 500 as retryable
findings.notes: Found by the staging certification runner (development run against the isolated QA tenant, before any migration of this branch was applied): refusals with SQLSTATE 55000 came back as HTTP 500. The API maps the whole SQLSTATE class 55 to 500 and that mapping is not configurable. The SQLSTATE does arrive in the response body, and the Panel already classifies by it for 42501, 22023, 23514, 23505, P0001 and P0002: it simply does not know 55000, so classifyRpcError (js/repositories/supabase-business-repository.js) and the two outbox result builders in js/production-operations.js answer retryable for a final refusal. The fix is in the client (three places, one shared predicate) and it changes the web release identity (asset digest and cache name), so it travels with the web release and was not put on this backend branch. Remapping the 213 existing refusals in the database would change the contract of dozens of functions and of every client that reads the code. This branch did not add new behaviour here: its new refusals follow the convention of the function they live in, and the delivery-coverage refusal of 20261001216000 uses 22023, which the client already shows as a message.

findings.title: The PAYMENT_APPROVED_WITHOUT_ORDER alert resolved itself when the same approved payment was read again, with the order still missing
